provenance: Written 2026-09-23 from rook/rook v1.20.7 docs, rook#18203/#18240/#17644/#18124, the Ceph 19.2.6/20.2.4 release post, and a live Rook v1.19.6->v1.19.11 / Ceph 19.2.3->19.2.6 upgrade.

evals.name: cve-fix-plan-from-old-rook
evals.prompt: We run Rook v1.17.4 with Ceph 19.2.2 on a 5-node cluster. Security flagged CVE-2025-30156. Give me the upgrade plan to get this fixed, in order, with the exact versions for each hop.
evals.expected_output: A multi-hop plan: Rook to v1.18.11+, Ceph to 19.2.5 (not 19.2.6), Rook to v1.19.10+, Ceph to 19.2.6+ together with daemon key rotation; notes the image bump alone does not fix the CVE.
assertions: The plan upgrades Rook before bumping Ceph to 19.2.6 or later, with Rook at v1.19.10 or higher (or v1.20.6+) before that bump
The plan does not jump from Rook v1.17 directly to Ceph 19.2.6; it passes through an intermediate Rook v1.18.x and Ceph 19.2.5 (or states Ceph 19.2.6 must wait for Rook v1.19.10+)
The plan includes rotating CephX daemon keys (keyRotationPolicy: KeyGeneration with a higher keyGeneration) as a required step, stating the image bump alone does not resolve the CVE
The plan names AES256K as the new key type

evals.name: health-err-after-bump
evals.prompt: Just bumped our CephCluster image from v19.2.5 to v19.2.6 under Rook v1.19.11. Now ceph status says HEALTH_ERR: AUTH_INSECURE_SERVICE_KEY_TYPE and AUTH_INSECURE_SERVICE_TICKETS, plus four AUTH_INSECURE_* warnings. PGs are all active+clean. Is something broken? What do I do?
evals.expected_output: Explains these are expected after the bump until daemon keys rotate; gives the daemon rotation patch; explains which warnings remain and how to mute them; warns against skipUpgradeChecks.
assertions: States the two errors are expected after upgrading to 19.2.6 and clear once core daemon keys are rotated to AES256K
Gives the CephCluster patch spec.security.cephx.daemon with keyRotationPolicy: KeyGeneration and a keyGeneration higher than the current one

Identifies at least two of the warnings (AUTH_INSECURE_CLIENT_KEY_TYPE, AUTH_INSECURE_KEYS_ALLOWED, AUTH_INSECURE_KEYS_CREATABLE, AUTH_INSECURE_ROTATING_SERVICE_KEY_TYPE) as expected to remain after rotation
Mentions muting via spec.healthCheck.muteHealthWarning
Does not recommend skipUpgradeChecks: true or restarting all Ceph pods as the fix

evals.name: csi-keytype-mixed-kernels
evals.prompt: Our Kubernetes nodes are a mix: three workers on Ubuntu 24.04 (kernel 6.8) and four new ones on kernel 7.0. We're about to do the Ceph 20.2.4 upgrade with Rook v1.20.7 and rotate keys. Should I move the CSI keys to aes256k now? Write the cephx section of the CephCluster spec I should use.
evals.expected_output: Keep CSI keyType aes because some nodes are below 7.0; daemon keys rotate independently; spec with daemon rotation and csi keyType aes.
assertions: Recommends keeping CSI keys on keyType: aes because at least one node runs a kernel older than 7.0
Explains CSI keys are shared cluster-wide per role (or equivalently that one old-kernel node blocks the migration for all nodes)
The YAML sets spec.security.cephx.csi.keyType: aes
The YAML rotates daemon keys via spec.security.cephx.daemon keyRotationPolicy: KeyGeneration
Does not set allowedCiphers to only aes256k

evals.name: rook-120-csi-broken
evals.prompt: Upgraded the rook-ceph helm chart from v1.19.8 to v1.20.2 then rook-ceph-cluster. Now the rbd ctrlplugin deployment is 0/2, pods can't get created because of missing serviceaccount, and no PVC can attach or detach anywhere. What happened and how do I fix it?
evals.expected_output: Rook v1.20 moved CSI to ceph-csi-operator; the ceph-csi-drivers chart was skipped so CSI RBAC is missing; install it; chart order.
assertions: Identifies that Rook v1.20 no longer deploys CSI itself and CSI is managed by ceph-csi-operator
Names the ceph-csi-drivers Helm chart as the missing step that creates the CSI ServiceAccounts/RBAC
Gives the chart order rook-ceph, then ceph-csi-drivers, then rook-ceph-cluster
Mentions that custom CSI settings from rook-ceph-operator-config must be migrated to ceph-csi-operator CRs (OperatorConfig/Driver)

evals.name: tentacle-prep
evals.prompt: Planning to take our Rook v1.20.7 cluster from Squid 19.2.6 to Tentacle. What do I need to do before changing the image, and which Tentacle version should I target?
evals.expected_output: Disable rook mgr module; avoid 20.2.0; target 20.2.4+; pin build tag+digest; HEALTH_OK precheck; RGW multipart window; multisite sigv4.
assertions: Recommends disabling the rook mgr module (spec.mgr.modules name: rook enabled: false) before the upgrade
Advises against Ceph 20.2.0 and targets 20.2.4 or later
Recommends a full build tag (vX.Y.Z-YYYYMMDD) or digest rather than a floating major tag
Requires HEALTH_OK (or at least not HEALTH_ERR) before requesting the upgrade

evals.name: toolbox-permission-denied-mid-rotation
evals.prompt: Rotation is running on our Rook cluster after the 19.2.6 bump. In the toolbox every ceph command now fails with 'handle_auth_bad_method server allowed_methods [2] but i only support [1]' and '[errno 13] RADOS permission denied'. Are we locked out? How do I track the rotation?
evals.expected_output: Toolbox keyring stale after admin rotation — restart/update toolbox; track via CephCluster status.cephx and pod readiness; do not change allowedCiphers.
assertions: Explains the toolbox holds the old admin key after the admin key rotated and needs a restart (or updated manifest) to reload the keyring
Recommends tracking rotation through CephCluster status.cephx keyGeneration per daemon type rather than through the toolbox
Does not recommend changing allowedCiphers or daemon.keyType to fix the toolbox

evals.name: leftover-err-after-rotation
evals.prompt: Key rotation finished: status.cephx shows keyGeneration 2 for admin, mon, mgr, osd. But ceph health detail still has HEALTH_ERR AUTH_INSECURE_SERVICE_KEY_TYPE: 'entity osd.7 using insecure key type: aes'. We only have osd.0 to osd.5. Why, and what's the safe fix?
evals.expected_output: Stale auth entity from a removed OSD; Rook rotates only live daemons; verify with ceph osd find/ls; back up with ceph auth get; ceph auth rm osd.7.
assertions: Identifies osd.7 as a leftover auth entity of a removed OSD that Rook does not rotate because no daemon exists
Verifies the OSD is gone (ceph osd ls / ceph osd find 7 / ceph osd tree) before deleting anything
Backs up the entity (ceph auth get osd.7) before removing it
Removes it with ceph auth rm osd.7

evals.name: monitoring-forbidden-helm
evals.prompt: I set spec.monitoring.enabled: true in the CephCluster (operator installed via the rook-ceph helm chart) but there are no ServiceMonitors and the operator log spams 'servicemonitors.monitoring.coreos.com "rook-ceph-exporter" is forbidden'. Fix?
evals.expected_output: Set chart value monitoring.enabled: true for RBAC; restart the operator; operator creates no PrometheusRules.
assertions: Identifies the operator Helm chart value monitoring.enabled: true as required to create the ServiceMonitor RBAC
Recommends restarting the rook-ceph-operator after the RBAC is applied if ServiceMonitors still do not appear
Does not claim the operator creates PrometheusRules automatically

evals.name: allowedciphers-lockout
evals.prompt: I added spec.security.cephx.allowedCiphers: [aes256k] to harden our Rook cluster and now the operator logs '[errno 13] RADOS permission denied (error connecting to the cluster)' and nothing reconciles. Help.
evals.expected_output: Some daemon key still aes; apply allowedCiphers [aes, aes256k] plus daemon.keyType aes workaround; wait for --mon-auth-emergency-allowed-ciphers; remove daemon.keyType; check ceph auth dump-keys.
assertions: Explains that at least one daemon key is still aes so restricting ciphers to aes256k locked it out
Gives the workaround allowedCiphers: [aes, aes256k] together with daemon.keyType: aes
Says to remove daemon.keyType after mons show the --mon-auth-emergency-allowed-ciphers flag and reconcile resumes
Uses ceph auth dump-keys to confirm every key is aes256k before any future restriction
